# Status/Presence Indicators

Covers bot presence types, activity types, and how to display status. See
[citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## Update Presence (Opcode 3)

Bots set their presence by sending an Update Presence payload (opcode 3) over
the gateway. The Identify payload (opcode 2) also accepts an optional
`presence` field for initial status. [1] [10]

### Payload Structure

| Field | Type | Purpose | Source |
|-------|------|---------|--------|
| `since` | ?integer | Unix time (ms) when went idle; null if active | [10] |
| `activities` | array | List of activity objects | [10] |
| `status` | string | Status state | [10] |
| `afk` | boolean | Whether client is AFK | [10] |

## Status Types

| Status | Display | Behavior | Source |
|--------|---------|----------|--------|
| `online` | Green dot | Active and available | [10] |
| `idle` | Yellow dot | Away / AFK | [10] |
| `dnd` | Red dot | Do Not Disturb | [10] |
| `invisible` | Gray dot | Appears offline to others | [10] |
| `offline` | Gray dot | Completely disconnected | [10] |

A bot that is running and connected to the gateway appears `online` by default.
Setting `invisible` keeps the bot connected but appears offline. [10]

## Activity Types

| Type | Name | Display Format | Source |
|------|------|---------------|--------|
| 0 | Playing | "Playing {name}" | [10] |
| 1 | Streaming | "Streaming {name}" | [10] |
| 2 | Listening | "Listening to {name}" | [10] |
| 3 | Watching | "Watching {name}" | [10] |
| 4 | Custom | User-defined status | [10] |
| 5 | Competing | "Competing in {name}" | [10] |

Example activity object: `{"name": "Save the Oxford Comma", "type": 0}` [10]

### Bot-Specific Notes

- Streaming (type 1) typically requires a valid Twitch or YouTube URL in the
  `url` field to display the streaming indicator
- Custom status (type 4) availability for bots is undocumented in fetched
  sources — community sources suggest bots cannot set type 4, but this was not
  confirmed from official docs

## Presence Intent

The `GUILD_PRESENCES` intent (1 << 8) is a **privileged intent** required to
receive `PRESENCE_UPDATE` events from other users. [1]

This is only needed if the bot wants to **monitor other users' presence** — not
for setting its own presence. A personal bot that only displays its own status
does not need this intent. [1]

## Presence Update Rate Limits

The gateway rate limit of 120 events per 60 seconds applies to all outgoing
events including presence updates. [1]

The fetched sources do not document a presence-specific sub-limit. Community
sources commonly cite 5 presence updates per 60 seconds, but this was not
confirmed from official documentation.

## Use Cases for Personal Automation

| Use Case | Activity Type | Example |
|----------|--------------|---------|
| Show bot is running | Playing (0) | "Playing Task Monitor" |
| Show current task | Watching (3) | "Watching 3 pending tasks" |
| Music/audio integration | Listening (2) | "Listening to Podcast" |
| Status indicator | Online/Idle | Online when active, idle when no tasks |

Setting presence on startup (via the Identify payload's `presence` field [1])
provides an immediate visual indicator that the bot is operational.

## Gaps and Limitations

- Whether bots can use Custom status (type 4) was not confirmed from official
  sources — this is a commonly discussed community question
- Presence-specific update rate limits (distinct from the general 120/60s
  gateway limit) were not found in fetched sources
- The Streaming activity type's URL requirement was not confirmed from the
  fetched gateway events page [10]
- Rich Presence SDK rate limits (1 per 15 seconds, from discovery phase) were
  not verified — this SDK is separate from bot presence updates
